invoked_by.description: At least one. An empty list is not representable in a valid entry, because an uninvoked gate is not enforcement.

provenance.description: For a `released_binary` entry: the kernel commit the binary was built from, which is where the five limbs actually resolve. Absent on every other kind, and absent here it is a NAMED missing link: doctor reports the subscriber seat NOT CHECKED rather than inventing a chain.

FailingDirectionTest.description:
The test that proves the gate's FAILING direction.

VDS S-7(2)(2): a check whose failing direction is asserted nowhere has proven only its happy path. This field is not optional, which is how that condition is made structural rather than requested: an entry cannot be written without naming the test.

seeds.description:
What violation the test seeds, in one line, where a reviewer will see it.

VDS docs/GOAL.md is explicit that the failing-direction test proves the check CAN fail and not that the seeded violation is the one that matters. That remains a review question, and this line is what a reviewer reads to answer it.

Invocation.description: Something that runs the gate which is not the author choosing to run it. VDS S-7(2)(3).

blocking.description: False where the surface runs the gate but does not block on it.

reference.description: Where it is wired: a workflow file and job, a hook path and line, a package script name.

InvokedBy.description: What invoked the run. VDS S-7(2)(3) requires something other than the author choosing to run it, and VDS S-7(3) holds that a hook is not CI.

oneOf.description: The SUBSCRIBER seat's gate pin ([2026] VJS-CC-VIBE-DESIGN-SYSTEM 1). A subscriber holds no gate source; what it can witness is the released binary that judges it - `path` is that binary, `digest` its bytes, and `provenance` the kernel commit whose own enforcement lock resolves the five limbs the subscriber relies on transitively. `proves` is empty: the binary is not one proof kind, it is the runner of all of them.

A gate that GRADES rather than proves: it reads the proof records and reports whether the criteria are met. It has no ProofKind, so `proves` is empty for this kind, and that emptiness is correct rather than missing.

It exists because of BREACH-0006. `crates/vds-cli/src/doctor.rs` grades every criterion and was on NEITHER enforcement list: D2, D3 and D4 were each weakened and then strengthened in one day and no drift finding fired. Changing a proof trips the lock; changing the code that grades the proofs tripped nothing, which is the one place a weakening is invisible. The reporting surface needs the same protection as the thing it reports on.

ProofKind.description: The closed registry at VDS S-7(5).

oneOf.description: Every component referenced by any declared screen exists in the register.
The register agrees with the codebase and with Figma, both directions.
No screen uses an unregistered component. The anti-drift proof.
Every registered component's boundaries clear their floors in every theme.
Every required state of every registered component is drawn.
Each registered component's code counterpart matches its contract.
The two named records agree where the pin declares them aligned.
A component proposed for retirement has zero remaining consumers.
Each generated ledger is current with its source.
Each registered screen's required arrangement is the arrangement its authoritative frame draws. The only kind whose subject is a SCREEN.
Each registered surface's SHAPE is the one the design system specifies, and the count that does not comply is BOUNDED AND FALLING. The only kind that carries a DIRECTION rather than a threshold.

Timestamp.description: UTC, second resolution, trailing Z. The one canonical form VDS writes.
